data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's error-residue diagnostic is circular and fails the problem's demand to distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance. It defines compliance errors as 'items the checklist covers but the panel misinterprets' and genuine gain as errors 'outside the checklist's scope.' But a panel that merely complies with a checklist will also fail on items outside the checklist's scope—so the proposed distinguishing criterion (outside-scope errors) does not separate genuine gain from compliance. Meanwhile, 'trap items' that trip intuitive experts are presumably covered by the checklist, so failing them would be classified as a compliance error, yet a genuinely-reliable panel could also fail such items through misunderstanding rather than lack of reliability. The error-residue analysis thus provides no non-circular marker that uniquely identifies genuine reliability.
